claim_records.title: Noninjective measurement obstruction
claim_records.statement_tex:
Let \(M:X\to Y\) be a measurement map. Suppose there are two admissible objects \(f_0,f_1\in X\) with
\[
M f_0=M f_1
\]
and different edge packets. No recovery map \(R:Y\to\mathcal J\) can return the correct edge packet for both objects.
claim_records.proof_tex: The two objects produce the same datum \(y=Mf_0=Mf_1\). The map \(R\) has one value at \(y\). That value cannot equal two different edge packets.
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: Finite point samples do not see every edge
claim_records.statement_tex: Fix finitely many sample points in an interval. There is a nonzero indicator packet supported between two adjacent sample points that vanishes at every sample point. Hence arbitrary unknown edges cannot be recovered from those samples.
claim_records.proof_tex: Choose a nonempty open interval containing no sample point. Its indicator is nonzero, has two edges, and is zero at every sampled coordinate.
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: Intersection obstruction
claim_records.statement_tex:
Let \(\mathcal S\) and \(\mathcal J\) be linear subspaces of an ambient vector space. If
\[
\mathcal S\cap\mathcal J\ne\{0\},
\]
then the decomposition \(f=s+j\) is not unique.
claim_records.proof_tex:
Take a nonzero \(h\in\mathcal S\cap\mathcal J\). Then
\[
f=s+j=(s+h)+(j-h).
\]
Both pairs belong to \(\mathcal S\times\mathcal J\), and the pairs are different.
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: No uniform Lipschitz recovery over colliding edges
claim_records.statement_tex: Let the measurement vector contain finitely many Fourier moments. There is no inverse map from moments to edge locations with one Lipschitz constant valid for all distinct edge configurations.
claim_records.proof_tex: The moment vector of the two-edge packet tends to the moment vector of the zero packet as \(\delta\to0\). The edge parameter does not converge to an ordinary two-edge parameter with fixed separation. Any uniform Lipschitz inverse would force a fixed nonzero edge displacement to be bounded by a constant times a measurement difference that tends to zero.

claim_records.title: Universal finite-dictionary recovery
claim_records.statement_tex:
The following statements are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Every \(s\)-sparse edge coefficient vector is uniquely determined from \(A\alpha\).
\item
\[
\Ker A\cap\{h:\norm{h}_0\le2s\}=\{0\}.
\]
\item Every set of at most \(2s\) columns of \(A\) is linearly independent.
\item
\[
\spark(A)>2s.
\]
\end{enumerate}
When these conditions hold, the solution of
\[
\boxed{
\min_{\alpha}\norm{\alpha}_0
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
A\alpha=\RS y
}
\]
is the true edge coefficient vector for every noise-free observation in the class.
claim_records.proof_tex:
Assume statement 2. Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be \(s\)-sparse and satisfy \(A\alpha=A\beta\). Then \(h=\alpha-\beta\) lies in \(\Ker A\), and \(\norm{h}_0\le2s\). Statement 2 gives \(h=0\), hence \(\alpha=\beta\).

Conversely, if statement 2 fails, choose a nonzero \(h\in\Ker A\) with \(\norm{h}_0\le2s\). Split the support of \(h\) into two disjoint sets of size at most \(s\). Write
\[
h=\alpha-\beta
\]
with \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) supported on those two sets. Then \(A\alpha=A\beta\) even though \(\alpha\ne\beta\). Universal uniqueness fails.

Statements 2, 3, and 4 are the standard equivalent definitions of the spark condition. The optimization claim follows because the true \(s\)-sparse vector is feasible and no other vector with at most \(s\) nonzero entries can be feasible.

claim_records.title: Finite-dictionary noise bound
claim_records.statement_tex:
Suppose
\[
y=s_0+D\alpha_0+\eta,
\qquad
\norm{\RS\eta}_2\le\varepsilon,
\qquad
\norm{\alpha_0}_0\le s.
\]
Let \(\widehat\alpha\) satisfy
\[
\norm{\widehat\alpha}_0\le s
\]
and
\[
\norm{A\widehat\alpha-\RS y}_2\le\varepsilon.
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{
\norm{\widehat\alpha-\alpha_0}_2
\le
\frac{2\varepsilon}{\gamma_{2s}}.
}
\]
Consequently,
\[
\norm{D(\widehat\alpha-\alpha_0)}_2
\le
\frac{2\norm{D}\varepsilon}{\gamma_{2s}}.
\]
claim_records.proof_tex:
Put \(h=\widehat\alpha-\alpha_0\). Its support has size at most \(2s\). By the triangle inequality,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\norm{Ah}_2
&\le
\norm{A\widehat\alpha-\RS y}_2
+
\norm{\RS y-A\alpha_0}_2\\
&\le2\varepsilon.
\end{aligned}
\]
The definition of \(\gamma_{2s}\) gives
\[
\gamma_{2s}\norm{h}_2\le\norm{Ah}_2.
\]
Combining the two estimates proves the first bound. The packet bound follows by applying \(D\).
claim_records.publication_repair: handle s=0 and empty coefficient space separately

claim_records.title: Support recovery by thresholding
claim_records.statement_tex:
If
\[
\min_{k\in\supp\alpha_0}|(\alpha_0)_k|
>
\frac{4\varepsilon}{\gamma_{2s}},
\]
then thresholding \(\widehat\alpha\) at \(2\varepsilon/\gamma_{2s}\) recovers the true support.
claim_records.proof_tex: Every coordinate error is at most the \(\ell^2\) error. True nonzero coefficients remain above the threshold, while true zero coefficients remain below it.

claim_records.title: Edge derivative packet
claim_records.proof_tex:
Let \(\varphi\) be a smooth periodic test function. Integrating by parts on each constant segment gives
\[
-\int_0^{2\pi}j(x)\varphi'(x)\,dx
=
\sum_{\ell=1}^{r}
\bigl(j(\tau_\ell^+)-j(\tau_\ell^-)\bigr)
\varphi(\tau_\ell).
\]
The coefficient of \(\varphi(\tau_\ell)\) is the jump amplitude \(a_\ell\). This is exactly the action of the stated sum of Dirac masses.
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: Hankel rank equals the number of active jumps
claim_records.proof_tex: The matrix \(V_q\) has full column rank because the nodes \(z_\ell\) are distinct. The diagonal matrix is invertible because every \(a_\ell\) and \(z_\ell\) is nonzero. The transpose \(V_q^{\mathsf T}\) has full row rank. Since \(V_q\) is injective on \(\C^r\), multiplication on the left cannot reduce the rank of the full-row-rank product of the remaining two factors. Therefore the product has rank \(r\).
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: Recovery of an unknown edge count
claim_records.statement_tex:
Suppose only an upper bound \(L\) is known. Construct \(H_L\) from \(2L-1\) consecutive moments. In exact arithmetic,
\[
r=\rank H_L.
\]
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: Exact location recovery
claim_records.statement_tex:
Under the hypotheses above, \(2r\) consecutive high-frequency moments determine \(Q\) uniquely. The roots of \(Q\) are exactly
\[
z_\ell=\e^{-\ii\tau_\ell}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{
\tau_\ell=-\arg z_\ell\pmod{2\pi}
}
\]
recovers every unknown edge location.
claim_records.proof_tex: The Hankel system has one solution because \(H_r\) is invertible. The true monic polynomial satisfies the system, so the computed polynomial equals the true polynomial. Its roots are the distinct values \(z_\ell\).
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: Exact jump-amplitude recovery
claim_records.statement_tex: The recovered locations and any \(r\) consecutive moments determine the jump amplitudes uniquely.
claim_records.proof_tex:
Factor the matrix as
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
1&\cdots&1\\
z_1&\cdots&z_r\\
\vdots&&\vdots\\
z_1^{r-1}&\cdots&z_r^{r-1}
\end{pmatrix}
\diag(z_1^{n_0},\ldots,z_r^{n_0}).
\]
Both factors are invertible.

claim_records.title: Universal unknown-edge recovery in \(\EdgeClass\)
claim_records.statement_tex:
Fix upper bounds \(K\) and \(L\). Let \(f\in\EdgeClass\) have \(r\le L\) distinct active jumps. Assume the jump amplitudes are nonzero. Suppose the Fourier coefficients
\[
\widehat f(n)
\]
are known for
\[
-K\le n\le K
\]
and for the \(2L\) consecutive positive indices
\[
K+1,
K+2,
\ldots,
K+2L.
\]
Then the following objects are determined uniquely and can be constructed by finite linear algebra.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The actual number of jumps \(r\).
\item Every off-grid jump location \(\tau_\ell\).
\item Every jump amplitude \(a_\ell\).
\item The canonical zero-mean edge packet \(j\).
\item Every background Fourier coefficient \(\widehat s(n)\).
\item The complete signal \(f=s+j\).
\end{enumerate}
claim_records.proof_tex:
Form the high-frequency moments
\[
m_n=2\pi\ii n\widehat f(n).
\]
Since \(n>K\), these equal the edge moments. Build the \(L\times L\) Hankel matrix. Its rank is the true number \(r\). Use the leading \(r\times r\) Hankel system to recover the monic annihilating polynomial. Its distinct roots yield the locations. The Vandermonde system yields the jump amplitudes. Periodic integration with zero mean yields \(j\). Subtraction from the low Fourier modes yields \(s\). Their sum is \(f\).

claim_records.title: Finite-rate measurement count
claim_records.statement_tex: The high-frequency edge information requires \(2L\) complex Fourier coefficients. The smooth packet requires \(2K+1\) low-frequency coefficients. Thus the declared class is reconstructed from a number of coefficients that grows linearly in the number of edge and background degrees of freedom.

claim_records.title: Gibbs-free exact synthesis
claim_records.statement_tex:
Under the hypotheses of the universal off-grid recovery theorem, the resolved reconstruction satisfies
\[
\widehat f_{\mathrm{resolved}}=f.
\]
In particular, the final signal has no Gibbs overshoot or undershoot.
claim_records.proof_tex:
The recovery theorem gives the exact locations and amplitudes, hence \(\widehat j=j\). It also gives every low-frequency background coefficient, hence \(\widehat s=s\). Therefore
\[
\widehat f_{\mathrm{resolved}}
=\widehat s+\widehat j
=s+j=f.
\]
The conclusion concerns the synthesized object. A plot of the truncated Fourier series may still show Gibbs ringing, but that approximation is no longer the reconstruction used by the model.
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: Deterministic root-disk certificate
claim_records.statement_tex:
If
\[
\sup_{|z-z_j|=\rho}|E_Q(z)|<m_j(\rho)
\]
for every \(j\), then \(\widetilde Q\) has exactly one root in each disk \(D_j\). Hence the recovered roots can be matched to the true roots with error less than \(\rho\).
claim_records.proof_tex: On the boundary of \(D_j\), the perturbation has smaller modulus than \(Q\). Rouché's theorem gives the same number of zeros inside the disk. Since \(Q\) has exactly one simple zero there, so does \(\widetilde Q\).
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: No separation-free stability
claim_records.statement_tex:
Fix finitely many Fourier indices. There is no constant \(C\) such that every two-jump periodic edge packet obeys
\[
\dist(\text{edge parameters},0)
\le
C\norm{\text{measured moments}}.
\]
claim_records.proof_tex: Use the opposite-jump family above. The parameter vector retains two nonzero unit jumps while the finite moment vector tends to zero as \(\delta\to0\).

claim_records.title: Shared-edge multichannel recovery
claim_records.statement_tex: If the stacked recurrence matrix has column rank \(r\), then the common annihilator is unique. Its roots recover every shared location. Channelwise Vandermonde solves then recover the amplitudes in each channel.
claim_records.proof_tex: Each channel supplies linear equations for the same recurrence coefficients. Full column rank makes the stacked solution unique. The root and amplitude steps are then the same as in the scalar theorem.
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: Confluent annihilation
claim_records.statement_tex:
Every sequence of the form above is annihilated by
\[
\boxed{
Q(E)
=
\prod_{\ell=1}^{r}(E-z_\ell)^{d+1},
}
\]
where \(E\) is the forward-shift operator on the moment index.
claim_records.proof_tex: For one term \(n^qz^n\), the operator \(E-z\) lowers the polynomial degree by one while retaining the exponential factor. Applying it \(q+1\) times gives zero. The product over all locations annihilates every term.
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: Exact order from Hankel rank
claim_records.statement_tex:
Assume the aliased nodes $u_1,\ldots,u_L$ are distinct and the coefficients $b_\ell$ are nonzero. If $R,C\ge L$, then
\[
\boxed{\rank H_0=L.}
\]
claim_records.proof_tex: Both Vandermonde factors have full column rank, and the diagonal coefficient matrix is invertible. The rank of their product is therefore $L$.
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: Order recovery under a singular-value gap
claim_records.statement_tex:
Let
\[
H=H_0+E,
\qquad
\rank H_0=L.
\]
If
\[
\norm E_2<\frac12\sigma_L(H_0),
\]
then any threshold $t$ satisfying
\[
\norm E_2<t<\sigma_L(H_0)-\norm E_2
\]
selects exactly $L$ singular values of $H$.
claim_records.proof_tex:
Weyl's singular-value perturbation inequality gives
\[
\sigma_L(H)\ge\sigma_L(H_0)-\norm E_2>t
\]
and
\[
\sigma_{L+1}(H)\le\norm E_2<t.
\]
The threshold therefore separates the signal rank from the defect tail.
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: Exact multi-offset phase
claim_records.statement_tex:
If
\[
c_r=bz^r,
\qquad
b\ne0,
\qquad
\abs z=1,
\]
then
\[
\boxed{\Phi(c)=z.}
\]
claim_records.proof_tex:
Each adjacent product is
\[
\overline{c_r}c_{r+1}=\abs b^2z.
\]
Hence
\[
S(c)=R\abs b^2z,
\]
and normalization gives $z$.
claim_records.publication_repair: require at least one adjacent product R>=1
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: Deterministic phase perturbation
claim_records.statement_tex:
Suppose
\[
c_r=bz^r+e_r,
\qquad
\abs z=1,
\qquad
\abs{e_r}\le\varepsilon.
\]
Let
\[
A=R\abs b^2,
\qquad
\delta=R(2\abs b\varepsilon+\varepsilon^2).
\]
If $\delta<A$, then $S(c)\ne0$ and
\[
\boxed{
\abs{\Phi(c)-z}
\le
\frac{2\delta}{A}
=
\frac{4\varepsilon}{\abs b}
+2\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{\abs b}\right)^2.
}
\]
claim_records.proof_tex:
Write
\[
S(c)=A z+E.
\]
Expanding each adjacent product gives
\[
\abs E\le R(2\abs b\varepsilon+\varepsilon^2)=\delta.
\]
Since $\delta<A$, the perturbed sum is nonzero. For any nonzero $w$ and $v=Az$,
\[
\left|\frac{w}{\abs w}-z\right|
\le
\left|\frac{w}{\abs w}-\frac{w}{A}\right|
+
\left|\frac{w-v}{A}\right|
\le
\frac{2\abs{w-v}}{A}.
\]
Substitute $w=S(c)$.
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: Exact validation
claim_records.statement_tex:
If $c_r=bz^r$ with $b\ne0$, then
\[
V(c,z)=0.
\]
Conversely, if $V(c,\widetilde z)=0$ and $c_0\ne0$, then
\[
c_r=c_0\widetilde z^r
\]
for every $r$.
claim_records.proof_tex:
The forward statement is immediate. For the converse, zero residual gives
\[
c_{r+1}=\widetilde zc_r.
\]
Induction gives the geometric progression.
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: Candidate separation
claim_records.statement_tex:
The $N$ roots of a nonzero complex number with fixed modulus are separated on their common circle by chord distance
\[
2r\sin\left(\frac\pi N\right),
\]
where $r$ is the root modulus.
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: Branch-margin criterion
claim_records.statement_tex:
Let $\abs z=1$ and $u=z^N$. Normalize a nonzero aliased estimate by
\[
\bar u=\frac{\widehat u}{\abs{\widehat u}}.
\]
Among the $N$ roots of $\bar u$, let $\rho$ be the one corresponding continuously to $z$. Let $\widetilde z$ be a coarse phase estimate. If
\[
\boxed{
\abs{\widetilde z-z}+\abs{\rho-z}
<
\sin\left(\frac\pi N\right),
}
\]
then the root of $\bar u$ nearest to $\widetilde z$ is $\rho$.
claim_records.proof_tex:
Every incorrect root is at least $2\sin(\pi/N)$ from $\rho$. The triangle inequality gives
\[
\abs{\widetilde z-\rho}
\le
\abs{\widetilde z-z}+\abs{z-\rho}
<
\sin(\pi/N).
\]
Every other root is farther than $\sin(\pi/N)$ from $\widetilde z$. Thus $\rho$ is the unique nearest root.
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: One-order root gain
claim_records.statement_tex:
Let $\abs u=1$, let $\bar u$ be a unit-modulus perturbation, and let $\rho$ be the corresponding branch of the $N$th root. If
\[
\abs{\bar u-u}\le\eta<2,
\]
then
\[
\boxed{
\abs{\rho-z}
\le
2\sin\left(
\frac{1}{N}\arcsin\frac\eta2
\right)
\le
\frac{2}{N}\arcsin\frac\eta2.
}
\]
claim_records.proof_tex: The angular perturbation of $u$ is at most $2\arcsin(\eta/2)$. Taking the corresponding $N$th root divides that angular perturbation by $N$. Convert the result back to chord distance.
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: Rate-preserving lifting
claim_records.statement_tex:
Fix $p\ge0$. Suppose a selected decimation $N$ satisfies the following estimates for each edge:
\[
\abs{\widehat u-u}\le C_uN^{-p-1},
\]
\[
\max_r\abs{\widehat b_r-b_r}\le C_bN^{-p-1},
\]
and
\[
\abs{b_0}\ge b_{\min}>0.
\]
Assume the branch-margin criterion holds for sufficiently large $N$. Then the lifted node estimate satisfies
\[
\boxed{
\abs{\widehat z-z}=O(N^{-p-2}).
}
\]
The corresponding location error satisfies the same order.
claim_records.proof_tex:
The phase perturbation theorem gives
\[
\abs{\widetilde z-z}=O(N^{-p-1}).
\]
For $p\ge0$, this is eventually smaller than the candidate spacing scale $N^{-1}$ whenever the constants and selected decimation satisfy the branch margin. The correct branch is therefore selected. The one-order root lemma then gives
\[
\abs{\widehat z-z}
\le
\frac{C}{N}\abs{\widehat u-u}
=O(N^{-p-2}).
\]
On the unit circle, angular and chord errors are locally equivalent.
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: Oracle-equivalent branch selection
claim_records.statement_tex: Under the branch-margin hypothesis, the root selected by the offset phase is exactly the root that would be selected by an oracle supplying the correct jump neighborhood. Therefore the self-calibrated estimator inherits every location-error estimate proved for that oracle branch.
claim_records.proof_tex: The oracle and the offset estimator both select the unique candidate root lying inside the branch-margin neighborhood of the true phase. Uniqueness forces the two selected roots to coincide.
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: Smooth-tail interpretation
claim_records.statement_tex:
Under the Fourier-tail assumption,
\[
\abs{e_{qN+r}}=O(N^{-p-1})
\]
for fixed $q$ and $r$. On any compact admissible parameter class for which the decimated Prony map and its coefficient solve have uniformly bounded local inverses, the hypotheses of the rate-preserving lifting theorem hold.
claim_records.proof_tex:
The moment defect follows directly from
\[
\abs{e_n}=2\pi\abs n\abs{\widehat s(n)}.
\]
Distinct aliased nodes and nonzero amplitudes make the finite Prony Jacobian a full-rank confluent Vandermonde system. Uniform separation and amplitude bounds give a bounded local inverse on a compact admissible class.
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: Exact self-calibration in the bandlimited control class
claim_records.statement_tex:
Suppose the smooth packet is bandlimited below the first moment index used by the algorithm. Assume exact arithmetic, an admissible edge packet, enough moments for the Hankel and coefficient systems, and one tested decimation with distinct aliased nodes. Then the procedure recovers:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the exact jump count $L$
\item every aliased node $u_\ell$
\item every physical phase $z_\ell$
\item every jump location $\tau_\ell$
\item every jump amplitude $a_\ell$
\item the exact edge packet $j$
\item the exact smooth packet $s$
\end{enumerate}
No externally supplied jump neighborhood is required.
claim_records.proof_tex: The high derivative moments contain only the edge exponential sum. The Hankel rank is exactly $L$. Exact Prony recovery gives the distinct aliased nodes. Each offset Vandermonde solve gives the exact coefficient progression $b_{\ell,r}=b_{\ell,0}z_\ell^r$. The phase estimator returns $z_\ell$. The branch lift therefore selects the correct physical root. A final real Vandermonde solve with the zero-sum constraint gives the jump amplitudes. Subtracting the recovered edge Fourier coefficients leaves the smooth coefficients.
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: Explicit finite innovation budget
claim_records.statement_tex:
Assume the hypotheses of the exact self-calibration theorem and suppose the jump count satisfies $L\le L_{\max}$. Choose integers $N\ge2$ and $q_0\ge1$ so that $q_0N$ lies above the smooth bandwidth. Define
\[
\mathcal I_0
=
\{(q_0+q)N:0\le q\le2L_{\max}\}
\]
and
\[
\mathcal I_1
=
\{(q_0+q)N+1:0\le q<L_{\max}\}.
\]
If the aliased nodes $u_\ell=z_\ell^N$ are distinct, then the derivative moments indexed by
\[
\mathcal I_0\cup\mathcal I_1
\]
determine the unknown order, every physical phase, and every jump amplitude exactly. The high-frequency innovation budget is
\[
\boxed{
\abs{\mathcal I_0}+\abs{\mathcal I_1}
=3L_{\max}+1.
}
\]
This count does not include the low Fourier coefficients used afterward to reconstruct the smooth packet.
claim_records.proof_tex:
The $2L_{\max}+1$ base-channel moments form an $(L_{\max}+1)\times(L_{\max}+1)$ Hankel matrix of exact rank $L$, so the unknown order is recovered. Once $L$ is known, the first $2L$ base moments determine the annihilating polynomial and hence the distinct aliased nodes $u_\ell$. Solving the base Vandermonde system gives
\[
b_{\ell,0}=a_\ell u_\ell^{q_0}.
\]
The adjacent channel contains
\[
m_{(q_0+q)N+1}
=
\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}b_{\ell,0}z_\ell u_\ell^q.
\]
Its first $L_{\max}$ samples contain at least $L$ equations. The Vandermonde solve therefore gives $b_{\ell,0}z_\ell$, and division by the nonzero base coefficient gives $z_\ell$ directly. Finally,
\[
a_\ell=b_{\ell,0}u_\ell^{-q_0}.
\]
The zero-mean normalization fixes the additive constant of the edge packet. Subtracting its Fourier coefficients leaves the smooth packet.
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: Perturbed self-calibration for a non-bandlimited background
claim_records.statement_tex:
Let the smooth packet satisfy the Fourier-tail assumption and let the edge packet belong to a compact admissible class. Suppose a tested decimation satisfies the singular-gap condition, the local inverse bounds for the decimated Prony and coefficient systems, and the branch-margin condition. Then, for sufficiently large decimation scale,
\begin{align*}
\widehat L&=L,\\
\max_\ell\abs{\widehat\tau_\ell-\tau_\ell}_{\T}&\le C_\tau N^{-p-2},\\
\max_\ell\abs{\widehat a_\ell-a_\ell}&\le C_aN^{-p-1}.
\end{align*}
The constants depend on the smooth-tail bound, separation, amplitude bounds, selected sample pattern, and local inverse constants.
claim_records.proof_tex: The smooth moment defect is $O(N^{-p-1})$. The singular-gap theorem preserves the order. The local inverse bounds transfer this perturbation to the aliased nodes and offset coefficients. The rate-preserving lifting theorem gives the location estimate. The amplitude estimate follows from the uniformly conditioned real Vandermonde solve.
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: Resolved synthesis inequality
claim_records.proof_tex:
Using $f=s+j$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
f-\widehat f_M
&=s+j-A_M(s+j-\widehat j)-\widehat j\\
&=(s-A_Ms)+(I-A_M)(j-\widehat j).
\end{aligned}
\]
Apply the triangle inequality and the operator bound.
claim_records.review_scope: source scope and selected direct implications; not final companion reconciliation

claim_records.title: Exact edge packet
claim_records.statement_tex:
If $\widehat j=j$, then
\[
\boxed{
\norm{f-\widehat f_M}=\norm{s-A_Ms}.
}
\]
No jump packet is sent through the smooth global approximation.

claim_records.title: Confluent offset phase
claim_records.statement_tex: For a jump jet with a nonzero leading singular coefficient, the physical edge phase is the ratio of corresponding highest-degree confluent coefficients in two adjacent offset channels.
claim_records.proof_tex: The highest power of $q$ arises from the leading term of $P_\ell((q_0+q)N+r)$. Every factor other than $z_\ell^r$ is independent of the offset. Taking the ratio cancels the aliased node, amplitude, decimation power, and initial-block factor.

claim_records.title: Finite dictionary identifiability
claim_records.statement_tex:
Every $s$-sparse edge vector is uniquely determined from $R_By$ if and only if
\[
\ker A\cap\{h:\|h\|_0\le 2s\}=\{0\}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\spark(A)>2s.
\]
claim_records.proof_tex:
If two $s$-sparse vectors $\alpha_1$ and $\alpha_2$ give the same residualized observation, then
\[
A(\alpha_1-\alpha_2)=0
\]
and $\alpha_1-\alpha_2$ has at most $2s$ nonzero entries. The kernel condition forces equality. Conversely, a nonzero $2s$-sparse kernel vector can be split into the difference of two $s$-sparse vectors, giving two distinct edge packets with the same observation.
